articles.title: Is an HbA1c of 13% at diagnosis normal?
articles.description: An HbA1c of 13% is not uncommon when someone is first diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes because the condition develops rapidly, allowing blood sugar levels to remain very high for weeks or months before symptoms appear. According to endocrinologist Dr Pranav Ghody, an HbA1c of 13% reflects an average blood glucose level above 300 mg/dL and is often associated with excessive thirst, frequent urination, weight loss, fatigue, and blurred vision. While such high levels increase the risk of serious complications like diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), prompt insulin therapy, regular blood sugar monitoring, proper nutrition, diabetes education, and consistent follow-up can significantly improve blood sugar control and help patients lead healthy, active lives.
